author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell breaks down an exchange over RFK Jr.'s push to establish a new agency within the CDC specifically devoted to tracking vaccine injuries, and questions why legacy media outlets are inviting critics on air to slam the idea instead of welcoming more transparency. The pushback claims tracking injuries too closely could make the data look more dramatic than it really is and scare parents away from vaccinating their kids, but Russell points out the glaring irony, the same officials worried about children being put at risk seem far less focused on the far more direct danger of ongoing child trafficking rings. A sharp look at where the real priorities in this debate actually lie.

title: Why does tracking vaccine injuries scare them?

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to the reality of Covid vaccines now being given to six month old babies, raising concerns that doubt about vaccination is treated as something that simply cannot be allowed to exist, no matter how well funded or reasonable that doubt might be. He points to researchers like Kevin McCarran who claim to have found troubling components in the shots, arguing that any questioning gets shut down instantly rather than investigated. Russell agrees with a comparison to religious devotion, suggesting the reverence surrounding vaccination has started to resemble a cult more than a rational medical debate. He closes by asking a simple question, if the trials are as solid as claimed, why would the pharmaceutical industry ever be opposed to further investigation.
